q1: False. HTML comments are not rendered by the browser but are fully visible in the page's source code. Anyone can view them by selecting 'View Source.'
q2: <, >, &. These characters must be escaped because they have special meaning in HTML markup — < and > as tag delimiters, & as the start of character references.
q3: Copyright symbol. The entity © renders as the copyright symbol (©).
q4: The browser may interpret it as markup. When you type < literally, the browser may think it's the start of an HTML tag, which can break your page layout.
q5: Wrong case may not resolve correctly. Entity names are case-sensitive, so &Amp; is not the same as & and may not render as intended.
q6: <. The correct numeric character reference format starts with &# followed by the number and ends with ;.
q7: False. HTML comments cannot be nested. Attempting to nest comments will result in the first closing --> ending the entire comment block.
q8: . The entity   represents a non-breaking space, which prevents browsers from collapsing multiple spaces into one.
q9: &. The correct entity for the ampersand character is &. This is necessary because & itself starts character references.
q10: They are visible in page source. HTML comments are not rendered on the page but are fully visible to anyone who views the page source, making them unsuitable for sensitive information.
